title: Redis Cluster: every key hashes to one of 16 384 slots, each slot to one primary
caption: The client computes the slot itself and talks to the right primary directly; replicas take over if a primary fails.

steps.text: slot = CRC16(key) mod 16384. For {user42}:cart only the part in braces is hashed, so all of user 42's keys share one slot.
The client caches the slot → node map and sends each command straight to the owner. A wrong guess gets a MOVED reply with the new owner.
Each primary streams its writes to a replica. If a primary fails, its replica is promoted and takes over the same slots.
Scaling out means moving whole slots to a new primary. A single key never splits, so one viral key still lands on one node.

scenarios.name: Primary B fails
scenarios.summary: Replica B is promoted and takes over B's slots; for the few seconds of detection those slots are unavailable, and writes B hadn't shipped are lost.

steps.text: Primary B crashes. Requests for slots 5461–10922 fail; A's and C's slots carry on.
The other primaries notice B missing heartbeats (node timeout, ~15 s by default) and vote to promote replica B.
Replica B now owns the slots. Clients get MOVED on their next try and update their map. Writes B acked but hadn't copied are gone.
Until a new replica is attached, those slots have no copy: one more failure there loses them.

scenarios.name: Cross-slot command
scenarios.summary: Multi-key commands work only when all keys are in one slot. Keys that belong together need a shared hash tag.

steps.text: MGET user:1:cart user:2:cart: the two keys hash to slots on A and B.
The cluster refuses with CROSSSLOT: no node can answer for both keys at once, and transactions can't span nodes.
Fix: name keys {user1}:cart and {user1}:profile so they share a slot, or split the command per key in the client.

scenarios.name: Alternative: one primary
scenarios.summary: One primary plus replicas and Sentinel: every key on one node, so multi-key commands just work, but writes and memory are capped by that one machine.
scenarios.caption: Sentinel watches the primary and promotes a replica on failure; replicas can take read traffic.

steps.text: All keys live on one primary: no slots, no CROSSSLOT, MULTI and Lua across any keys.
Replicas copy everything and can serve reads that tolerate a little lag.
Sentinels agree when the primary is down and promote a replica.
Ceiling: one machine's RAM (tens of GB) and one thread's writes (~100k ops/s). Past that, shard: Redis Cluster.
